VERIFICATION

I, {appellant_name}, son/daughter/wife of {appellant_father_name}, aged about {appellant_age} years, the Appellant herein, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {lastParagraph} of the above appeal are true and correct to my personal knowledge, and matters of legal submission are believed true on advice of counsel. promptInstructions: Draft a Criminal Appeal under appropriate provision of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

APPELLATE FRAMEWORK in BNSS: S.415 — appeal from Sessions / Additional Sessions sentence to HC (was S.374(2) CrPC); S.416 — appeal by State against acquittal (was S.378 CrPC); S.417 — appeals from convictions and sentences passed by Assistant Sessions Judge / Magistrate of First Class in certain cases (sentence > 7 years to HC); S.418 — appeals from Magistrate convictions / sentences (other than above) to Sessions; S.419 — appeals by complainant in case of acquittal (with leave); S.420 — no appeal in certain cases (very minor sentences); S.421 — no appeal in petty cases.

TIME LIMITS (Limitation Act Schedule + BNSS): Appeal against conviction by Sessions to HC — 60 days (Art. 115); Appeal to Sessions from Magistrate — 30 days; Appeal by State against acquittal to HC — 90 days; Leave to appeal against acquittal by complainant — within 60 days. Always cross-check current limitation, especially time from receipt of certified copy (S.12(2) Limitation Act allows exclusion of period for obtaining certified copy).
Para 1: Description of parties — appellant, respondent, State.
Para 2: Impugned judgment details — trial court, date of judgment, sections of conviction / acquittal, sentence.
Para 3: Brief prosecution case as alleged.
Para 4: Trial proceedings — number of PWs and DWs, documents marked, charges framed.
Para 5: Trial court's reasoning (in brief, fairly stated).
Para 6: Appellate jurisdictional basis — quote applicable BNSS section.
Para 7: Limitation — confirm date of certified copy, date of filing, that appeal is within limitation; otherwise file companion S.5 Limitation Act application.
Para 8: GROUNDS OF APPEAL — itemised (a, b, c, d…) — each ground a single contention.

Para 9: Errors in appreciation of evidence: (i) PW-1 testimony — contradictions, infirmities, motive to falsely implicate, prior inconsistent statements u/S.180 / S.181 BNSS; (ii) PW-2 etc.; (iii) Documentary evidence — admissibility, authenticity, contents; (iv) Material objects — chain of custody.

Para 10: Errors of law: (a) misapplication of BNS section — ingredients not satisfied; (b) misapplication of BSA provisions — presumptions wrongly drawn; (c) procedural illegalities — non-compliance with S.180 BNSS statements, non-furnishing of chargesheet documents, denial of fair trial.

Para 11: Witness reliability principles — for accused appeal: Cite K. Ponnuswamy v. State of Tamil Nadu (2001) 6 SCC 674 — proof beyond reasonable doubt mandatory; Cite Sharad Birdhichand Sarda v. State of Maharashtra (1984) 4 SCC 116 — circumstantial evidence — five golden principles.
Para 12: Burden and standard of proof — for accused: Cite Sujit Biswas v. State of Assam (2013) 12 SCC 406 — distinction between 'may be' and 'must be'.
Para 13: Benefit of doubt — Cite Hari Charan Kurmi v. State of Bihar AIR 1964 SC 1184 — confessions and benefit of doubt; Manoj v. State of MP (2023) — recent principles.

Para 14: For State / complainant appeal against acquittal — higher threshold: Cite Chandrappa v. State of Karnataka (2007) 4 SCC 415 — five principles for appellate interference with acquittal; presumption of innocence reinforced; only if view of trial court 'perverse' or 'impossible'. Cite Rajesh Singh v. State of UP (2011) 11 SCC 444. Cite Mallappa v. State of Karnataka (2024) — recent reiteration.
Para 15: For complainant appeal: S.419(4) BNSS requires leave to appeal — must specifically seek leave at admission.

Para 16: Sentence-only appeal — Cite Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab (1980) 2 SCC 684 (death sentence — rarest of rare); Machhi Singh v. State of Punjab (1983) 3 SCC 470; for non-capital — Soman v. State of Kerala (2013) 11 SCC 382 (proportionality principles); reformative approach for first offenders; mitigating circumstances.
Para 17: Death sentence reference — automatic confirmation by HC under S.407 BNSS (was S.366 CrPC); appellant typically files appeal separately.

Para 18: Suspension of sentence — file separate application under S.430 BNSS (was S.389 CrPC). Cite Bhagwan Rama Shinde Gosai v. State of Gujarat (1999) 4 SCC 421 — principles for suspension of sentence pending appeal.
Para 19: Bail pending appeal — relate to suspension application.
Documents to enclose: certified copy of judgment, certified copy of sentence order, full trial court record (or appellant's set), index of witnesses, list of exhibits.
Filing process: Where appellant in custody, appeal can be filed through Superintendent of Jail (S.428 BNSS — was S.383 CrPC).
For young / first-time advocates: keep grounds focused — pick 5-8 strongest grounds rather than 30 generic ones.
Affidavit in support is mandatory.
Append Lawie disclaimer.

sections.description: Appeal from sentences of Court of Session / ASJ to HC (replaces S.374(2) CrPC)
Appeal by State Government against acquittal / sentence (replaces S.378 CrPC)
Appeals to HC from certain Magistrate convictions
Appeals from Magistrate convictions to Sessions Court (replaces S.374(3) CrPC)
Appeals by complainant against acquittal — leave required (replaces S.378(4) CrPC)
No appeal in certain cases — petty sentences
No appeal where accused pleads guilty
Petition of appeal by accused in jail (through Superintendent)
Suspension of sentence pending appeal; release on bail (replaces S.389 CrPC)
Confirmation of death sentence by HC
Substantive offence sections — use BNS numbers (not IPC)
Evidence law — replaces Indian Evidence Act 1872
Appeal from order of acquittal — 60 / 90 days
Appeal from sentence to HC — 60 days
Exclusion of time for certified copy

filing_checklist: Appeal (original + copies as per court rules)
Certified copy of sentence order (if separate)
Certified copies of charge framed, depositions, exhibits
Suspension of sentence application (separate, under S.430 BNSS)
Leave to appeal application (if S.419(4) applies)
If appellant in custody — through Jail Superintendent (S.428 BNSS)
Disclaimer slip — Lawie drafting assistance acknowledged
validation_rules: appellate_forum must match offence severity and forum hierarchy
judgment_date must be valid date in past

TIME-BAR CHECK: 30 days (Mag to Sessions); 60 days (Sessions to HC for conviction); 90 days (State against acquittal); 60 days (complainant against acquittal with leave). If exceeded, condonation needed.
offences_convicted must use BNS sections (warn if IPC sections detected)
If appellant_status = complainant_against_acquittal_s419, leave_required must be true
If suspension_of_sentence_sought=true, flag separate S.430 application needed
advocate_enrollment must match Bar Council format
